items.title: Section: The Buddha's Parable of the Oil Bowl and the Executioner's Sword

items.zh: 世尊依此所緣境相，密意說言：汝等苾芻，當知眾善。言眾善者，謂於大眾共集會中，盛壯美色。即此眾善最殊勝者，謂於多眾大集會中，歌舞倡伎。假使有一智慧丈夫，從外而來，告一人曰：咄哉！男子！汝於今者，可持如是平滿鉢油，勿令灩溢；經歷如是大眾中過，當避其間所有眾善，及諸最勝歌舞倡伎、大等生等。今有魁膾，露拔利劍隨逐汝行。若汝鉢油一滴墮地，此之魁膾，即以利劍當斬汝首，斷汝命根。
items.en: The World-Honoured One, with reference to this very object, spoke with hidden intent, saying: "Monks, you should know of 'the crowd's pleasures.' By this is meant, within a great assembly gathered together, youthful beauty in its prime; and the very finest of these pleasures — song, dance, and entertainers, amid the great multitude. Suppose a wise man comes from outside and says to another: 'Listen! Take this bowl, brimful of oil, and do not let it spill. You must pass straight through this great assembly, avoiding all its pleasures — the finest song, dance, and entertainers, and the great and lesser folk alike. Behind you, even now, an executioner follows with sword drawn. Should a single drop of your oil fall to the ground, this executioner will strike off your head and sever your life on the spot.'"

items.zh: 苾芻！汝等於意云何？是持鉢人，頗不作意專心油鉢、拔劍魁膾、不平地等，而能作意觀視眾善，及諸最勝歌舞倡伎大等生耶？不也，世尊！何以故？
是持鉢人，既見魁膾，露拔利劍隨逐而行，極大怖畏，專作是念：我所持鉢油既彌滿，經是眾中極難將度；脫有一滴當墮地者，定為如是拔劍魁膾當斬我首，斷我命根。是人爾時，於彼眾善及諸最勝歌舞倡伎、大等生等，都不作意、思念、觀視，唯於油鉢專心作意而正護持。如是苾芻！我諸弟子，恭敬殷重，專心憶念修四念住，當知亦爾。
items.en: "Seeing the executioner following with sword drawn, this man, in great terror, thinks only: 'My bowl is brimful of oil, and passing through this crowd will be extremely difficult; should even one drop fall, this sword-bearing executioner will surely strike off my head and sever my life.' At that time, this man pays no attention whatsoever to the crowd's pleasures … giving his whole attention only to guarding the oil bowl correctly." "Just so, monks: my disciples, with reverence and earnestness, single-mindedly holding the four foundations of mindfulness in mind, should be understood to be exactly the same."

items.zh: 言眾善者，喻能隨順貪欲纏等隨煩惱法。於中最勝歌舞倡伎，喻能隨順尋思戲論躁擾處法。大等生等，喻色相等十種相法。智慧丈夫，喻瑜伽師。平滿油鉢，喻奢摩他所安住心，能令身心輕安潤澤，是奢摩他義。露拔利劍隨行魁膾，喻先所取諸相、尋思、隨煩惱中諸過患相。專心將護，不令鉢油一滴墮地，喻能審諦周遍了知亂不亂相之所攝受奢摩他道。

items.title: Section: Equipoise — Not Even One Moment of Distraction

items.zh: 由是能令諸心相續、諸心流注；由精進力，無間策發。前後一味，無相、無分別，寂靜而轉；不起一心復緣諸相，或緣尋思及隨煩惱。
items.en: Through this, mind continues upon mind, mind flows upon mind; through the power of diligence, it is unceasingly roused. One taste from beginning to end, free of marks, free of discursive thought, it proceeds in tranquility — not a single moment of mind arises directed towards any mark, or towards discursive thought, or towards any secondary affliction.

items.zh: 是瑜伽師復應如是慇懃教誨於奢摩他初修業者。告言：

items.title: The Teacher's Further Guidance: When Stillness Brings Joy, and When to Switch to Insight

items.zh: 賢首！汝若如是精勤修習奢摩他道，如是方便，攝受正念、正知俱行有喜樂心，乃名善修奢摩他道。若復串習諸過失故，不能於中深心喜樂，極大艱辛勵力策發方現前者；還應速疾出無分別所緣境相，於有分別所緣境相繫念在前，如先所取諸不淨相。
items.en: "Excellent one! If you diligently cultivate the path of calm-abiding in this way, sustaining mindfulness and clear comprehension together with a joyful mind through such means, this is called skilfully cultivating the path of calm-abiding. But if, through habituated faults, you are unable to find deep joy in it, and it appears only through the greatest hardship and forced effort, you should then swiftly abandon the non-discriminating object and instead fix mindfulness on a discriminating object — such as the marks of impurity previously grasped."

items.zh: 汝今復應作意思惟，先應用彼唯隨相行毘鉢舍那，或觀青瘀，或觀膿爛，廣說乃至觀骨、觀鎖，或觀骨鎖。

items.title: Section: Generating Vivid Understanding — From One Corpse to Boundless Space

items.zh: 汝於如是初修觀時，於一青瘀，廣說乃至於一骨鎖，當起勝解。若於其中已串修習，觀道明淨，於所緣相明了勝解相續轉時，復應於二、於三、於四、於五、於十、二十、三十、四十、五十，或百青瘀、或千青瘀，乃至一切諸方諸維所有青瘀，起無量行遍一切處無間勝解，於中乃至無有容受一杖端處。
items.en: "When you first cultivate insight in this way, you should generate vivid understanding of a single instance of discoloration, and so on at length, up through a single bone-chain. Once you have habitually practised this, and the contemplation has become clear and pure, with the object's understanding continuing on lucidly, you should then extend to two, three, four, five, ten, twenty, thirty, forty, fifty, a hundred, or a thousand instances of discoloration, up through all instances of discoloration in every direction and quarter — generating boundless, uninterrupted vivid understanding pervading every place, until there is not even room enough for the tip of a walking staff."

items.zh: 如於青瘀，如是乃至骨鎖亦爾。

blocks.text: The Buddha's famous parable of the bowl of oil, then the teacher's guidance on when to practise stillness and when insight. A short passage (0460c13) is untranslated.

The Buddha spoke of "the crowd's pleasures": a great gathering, youthful beauty, the finest song and dance. "A man is given a bowl brimful of oil and told: carry this through the crowd without spilling a drop; behind you walks an executioner with sword drawn; if one drop falls, he will strike off your head." Venerable Miào Jìng: the wise man who gives the instruction "represents the yoga teacher: who is the wise man? Your teacher." The man's attention never leaves the bowl. So the meditator's mind stays on its object, untouched by the crowd of attractions.

"Mind continues upon mind, mind flows upon mind; through the power of diligence it is unceasingly roused. One taste from beginning to end, free of marks, free of discursive thought." "Not a single moment of mind arises directed towards any mark."

"If you cultivate the path of calm in this way, with a joyful mind, this is skilful. But if, through habituated faults, you cannot find deep joy in it, and it appears only through great effort", then "swiftly abandon the non-discriminating object and fix mindfulness on a discriminating one": switch to insight.

subs.head: From one corpse to boundless space

blocks.text: "First generate vivid understanding of a single instance of discoloration, up through a single bone chain." When it is clear, extend it: two, three, up to all directions, "until there is not even room for the tip of a walking staff".

quiz.q: In the oil-bowl story, how does it end, according to Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: the minister minded only the bowl, saw nothing else, succeeded, and was made prime minister
quiz.why: "Take this bowl, brimful of oil, and do not let it spill." Master Cháng Bǎi: because the minister attended only to the oil bowl and saw none of those sights, he succeeded in the end, and the king appointed him prime minister.

quiz.q: In the parable, whom does the "wise man" represent, according to Venerable Miào Jìng?
quiz.why: "Suppose a wise man comes from outside and says to another." Venerable Miào Jìng: the wise man represents the yoga teacher — who is the wise man? Your teacher.

quiz.q: "Through diligence, unceasingly roused." How does Venerable Miào Jìng describe diligence?
options: never slack, never pausing — spurring oneself on
quiz.why: "Through the power of diligence, it is unceasingly roused." Venerable Miào Jìng: by the power of diligence, without laziness or interruption, you spur yourself on and arouse effort.

quiz.q: "Mindfulness and clear comprehension with a joyful mind — skilful calm." What does Venerable Miào Jìng say?
options: with joy in mindfulness and awareness — that's skilful calm; irritation is not joy
quiz.why: "Sustaining mindfulness and clear comprehension together with a joyful mind — this is called skilfully cultivating calm-abiding." Venerable Miào Jìng: with right awareness and mindfulness, a joyful mind — that is skilful calm; not irritation, which isn't joy.

quiz.q: If calm comes only with great strain, "swiftly leave the non-discriminating object for a discriminating one." What do the masters say?
options: Miào Jìng: the discriminating object is insight; Cháng Bǎi: neither calm nor insight must come first, nor any fixed method
quiz.why: "You should then swiftly abandon the non-discriminating object and instead fix mindfulness on a discriminating object — such as the marks of impurity previously grasped." Venerable Miào Jìng: the discriminating object is insight — fix mindfulness on it. Master Cháng Bǎi: so it's not fixed whether to do calm or insight first, nor which method to apply.

quiz.q: "When first cultivating insight, generate understanding of a single discoloration." What does Venerable Miào Jìng say?
options: observe with great strength, reflecting on its appearance
quiz.why: "When you first cultivate insight, you should generate vivid understanding of a single instance of discoloration, up through a single bone-chain." Venerable Miào Jìng: contemplate this discoloration with great strength, reflecting on its appearance.

quiz.q: Expanding until "not even room for a staff's tip" needs strong mindfulness. What did Venerable Miào Jìng often ask disciples, according to Master Cháng Bǎi?
quiz.why: "Until there is not even room enough for the tip of a walking staff." Master Cháng Bǎi: whenever Venerable Miào Jìng met disciples, he liked to ask: "Ah, so-and-so! Does your mindfulness have strength?"
